name: Coral Reef Aesthetics Rating
description: Underwater aesthetics survey from Marshall et al. (2019, PLOS ONE), built to give reef managers measurable indicators of beauty for the Great Barrier Reef. 1,417 Australians each rated 50 photos, drawn at random from a pool of 181, on a scale from 1 (really unattractive) to 10 (really attractive), after a few questions on age, gender, where they live, their experience with the Great Barrier Reef and their interest in coral reefs. The researchers had coded every photo low / medium / high on five candidate indicators: coral cover, coral pattern, coral topography, fish abundance and visibility. Topography, fish abundance and visibility predicted the ratings; coral cover and pattern did not. The template ships with the paper's photos: 175 unique images from S1 File (CC BY; photos by Matt Curnock, Paul Marshall and GBRMPA). Each file name carries the paper's indicator codes, e.g. gbr001_c3p2t2f3v3.jpg = coral cover 3, pattern 2, topography 2, fish 3, visibility 3, so you can rerun the paper's analysis (mean rating per photo, then ANCOVA or regression on the five indicators; ratings by gender, age, experience and interest). Differences from the original study: (1) the paper's pool of 181 included six duplicated photos; the template uses the 175 unique ones; (2) residence questions are generalised (Queensland / elsewhere in Australia / outside Australia; city vs rural or regional) and an "Other / prefer not to say" gender option is added; (3) the paper used a panel provider (Pollinate) for a representative Australian sample; recruit your own sample; (4) the qualitative key-informant interviews that produced the indicators are not part of the template.
author: Marshall, Marshall, Curnock, Pert, Smith & Visperas
